slides.headline: October 26, 1890: a journalist was born who gave Bhagat Singh his first writing job - and died trying to stop a riot.
Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi was born in Allahabad on October 26, 1890
slides.body: He founded the Hindi newspaper Pratap in 1913, campaigning for peasants and mill workers under British rule - work that got him prosecuted and jailed five separate times.

slides.headline: On March 25, 1931, he was killed trying to rescue Hindus and Muslims trapped in Kanpur's communal riots.
slides.body: Nehru said of his death that "he taught in his death what we will find difficult to teach while living for many years." India later issued a commemorative stamp in his honour and named an annual journalism award after him.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat remembers that a free press was built by people who risked everything for it.
slides.body: Vidyarthi's five prison terms and the way he died are a reminder that institutional freedoms India now takes for granted were paid for, one newspaper and one life at a time.

sources.text: The Wire - The Editor Who Lived and Died for Communal Harmony
